chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man stands in salat (prayer) and intends to recite a surah,
but he recites: “Say: He is Allah, One,” and “Say: O disbelievers.”
“He may return from every surah except from ‘Say: He is Allah, One’ and ‘Say: O disbelievers.’”

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; the legal subject described in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer in which the recitation occurs
key_terms.سُورَةً: a surah; a chapter of the Qur'an being recited in prayer
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Surat al-Ikhlas, a specific Qur'anic surah exempted from switching away after beginning it
key_terms.قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ: Surat al-Kafirun, a specific Qur'anic surah exempted from switching away after beginning it
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: he returns; here meaning to go back or switch from the surah being recited

ai.seo_question: Can a person change the surah after starting recitation in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about recitation in salat (prayer). It states that one who has begun reciting a surah may switch from it, except if he has begun Surat al-Ikhlas or Surat al-Kafirun, from which he does not return.
